title: How Heavy Is the Night
description: How Heavy Is the Night in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 98, headed “The same”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How hea-vy is the night That hangs up-on our eyes, Till Christ with his re-viv-ing light, O-ver our souls a-rise!

lines: Till Christ with his reviving light,
To meet the wrath of heaven
Are all our thoughts and ways;
To hold our souls in vain;
He sets the sons of bondage free,
To bring us near to God,
Thy sovereign power, thy healing grace,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
